nrr:aiUseDeclaration.statement: We used Claude (Opus 4, 4.5, and 4.6) to help write, clean up, comment, and review our code, and we selectively incorporated its feedback. We also used Claude to suggest wording ideas and then chose which small phrases or sentence structure ideas to use, rearrange text to fit the structure of one of our pub templates, expand on summary text that we provided, and help clarify and streamline text that we wrote. Additionally, we chatted with Claude throughout the project to support ideation and analysis. We used Gemini (2.5 Pro) to review the publication to catch typos and discrepancies, and Cursor for tab completion while editing code.

nrr:applicabilityConditions.assay: spontaneous Raman spectroscopy, 785 nm excitation, desiccated wet cell pellets on stainless steel
nrr:applicabilityConditions.metric: multiclass Matthews correlation coefficient (MCC), bounded in [-1, +1], where +1 is perfect prediction, 0 is random guessing and negative values indicate systemic misclassification; computed per fold and reported as the median across folds
nrr:applicabilityConditions.models: random forest with 300 trees, and a support vector machine with an RBF kernel and C = 100; class weighting balanced; scikit-learn implementations; hyperparameters chosen empirically
nrr:applicabilityConditions.note: conclusions are specific to this sample-preparation protocol; desiccation is inherently variable and likely contributes to the plate-level batch effect
nrr:applicabilityConditions.processing: cosmic ray removal with the Whitaker-Hayes despiking algorithm, default parameters; background subtraction using a single consensus dark spectrum averaged across all three plates, deliberately not one per plate, to avoid injecting additional batch effects; quality control removing spectra whose mean background-subtracted intensity fell below an empirically determined threshold of 1,000 intensity units; Savitzky-Golay smoothing, then autofluorescence baseline subtraction with ModPoly, polynomial order five; cropping to the fingerprint region 300-1,800 cm-1 and area-under-the-curve normalization; outlier removal within each well by elbow detection on each spectrum's deviation from the group median
nrr:applicabilityConditions.replicates: three end-to-end biological replicates, produced by repeating sample preparation and imaging in triplicate with separate cell cultures, physical plates and imaging dates
nrr:applicabilityConditions.samplePreparation: wet cell pellets spotted onto stainless steel plates stamped with a 96-well layout and desiccated at room temperature and pressure for approximately 3 h
nrr:applicabilityConditions.strainDiversity: three standard lab strains and six knockout strains within two species; the authors note the strains may be too genetically similar to produce detectable spectral differences

nrr:confidence.basis: the batch effect is demonstrated directly by an adversarial task and is robust to classifier and batch-correction method; the strain negative rests on 248 spectra across nine closely related strains and is explicitly flagged by the authors as possibly not generalising

nrr:cost.note: 75 spectra acquired per strain across three plates, 248 retained after quality control; no monetary or compute cost is reported

@graph.nrr:hypothesis: Evaluate whether spontaneous Raman spectra can distinguish strains and species of yeast, and determine the extent to which batch effects from experimental variation confound such predictions.
nrr:invalidators: a strain panel with greater genetic diversity in which strain identity survives leave-one-replicate-out cross-validation
a sample-preparation protocol whose adversarial plate-prediction control is clean without correction
a batch-correction scheme applied within each training fold, which would make the corrected estimates valid for unseen plates
nrr:nextSteps: Incorporate at least three end-to-end replicates from the outset.
Include leave-one-replicate-out cross-validation in analysis workflows.
Include adversarial prediction tasks in which a model is trained to predict biologically meaningless variables such as replicate or plate identifiers.
nrr:openQuestions: How much of the residual strain-level signal loss is stochastic sample-level batch effect and how much is genuine absence of strain-specific Raman signatures?
@graph.nrr:outcomeSummary: Species identity is recoverable from the spectra (median MCC 0.97 under leave-one-plate-out cross-validation). Strain identity is not: it appears recoverable under standard cross-validation (0.79) but collapses when whole plates are held out (0.32), and an adversarial classifier predicts plate identity almost perfectly, showing that batch effects dominate.
nrr:provenanceNotes: Tagged 'No longer actively updating' rather than 'Iced'. There is no Icebox statement and no stated abandonment reason, so no abandonment reason is recorded.
The pub is CC BY 4.0 but the deposited code and data archive carries the MIT licence; the two differ within one study.

Self-declared analysis limitation carried on the corrected findings: The batch correction introduces an implicit train-test leakage, as it applies batch correction once to the full dataset rather than to each training fold separately. For leave-one-plate-out cross-validation this effect is severe, as the batch-effect dimension and the cross-validation dimension are identical. The batch-corrected leave-one-plate-out estimates are not valid estimates of generalization to fully unseen plates.

Only random-forest numbers are given numerically in the text. Figure 8 reports every combination of model and batch-correction method, and the authors state the medians were not meaningfully different; those combinations are recorded as a robustness finding rather than as separate measured values.
This is the only study in the corpus whose AI-use statement includes participation in ideation and analysis, not only in code and prose.
@graph.nrr:sourceLicense: CC BY 4.0 (pub); MIT (code and data archive)
@graph.nrr:successCriteria: Classification accuracy above chance under a cross-validation scheme that holds out whole experimental replicates, with an adversarial control showing that the model is not reading batch identity.

nrr:untriedBranches.description: Incorporate at least three end-to-end replicates from the outset.
Include leave-one-replicate-out cross-validation in analysis workflows.
Include adversarial prediction tasks in which a model is trained to predict biologically meaningless variables such as replicate or plate identifiers.
Repeat the strain task on a panel with greater genetic diversity; the authors state the negative result may not generalise to more divergent strains.
Repeat with a sample-preparation protocol that avoids desiccation, which the authors identify as a likely source of the plate-level batch effect.
